passages.text: Now the Feast of Unleavened Bread, called the Passover, was approaching, and the chief priests and scribes were looking for a way to put Jesus to death; for they feared the people.
passages.sermon:
The Feast of Unleavened Bread was coming soon.
People also called this feast the Passover.
The chief priests and the scribes wanted to kill Jesus.
They looked for a way to do this.
They feared the people.
passages.original: Ἤγγιζεν δὲ ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν ἀζύμων ἡ λεγομένη Πάσχα καὶ ἐζήτουν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τὸ πῶς ἀνέλωσιν αὐτόν ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ τὸν λαόν

passages.text: Then Satan entered Judas Iscariot, who was one of the Twelve.
passages.sermon: Judas Iscariot was one of the twelve disciples of Jesus.\r\nSatan entered Judas Iscariot.
passages.original: Εἰσῆλθεν δὲ Σατανᾶς εἰς Ἰούδαν τὸν καλούμενον Ἰσκαριώτην ὄντα ἐκ τοῦ ἀριθμοῦ τῶν δώδεκα

passages.text: And Judas went to discuss with the chief priests and temple officers how he might betray Jesus to them.
passages.sermon:
Judas was one of the twelve disciples of Jesus.
Satan entered Judas.
Judas went to the chief priests.
Judas also went to the temple officers.
Judas talked with them.
Judas discussed how he could hand Jesus over to them.
passages.original: καὶ ἀπελθὼν συνελάλησεν τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ στρατηγοῖς τὸ πῶς αὐτοῖς παραδῷ αὐτόν

passages.text: They were delighted and agreed to give him money.
passages.sermon: The chief priests and temple officers listened to Judas.\r\nThey felt joy.\r\nThey decided to give Judas money.
passages.original: καὶ ἐχάρησαν καὶ συνέθεντο αὐτῷ ἀργύριον δοῦναι

passages.text: Judas consented, and began to look for an opportunity to betray Jesus to them in the absence of a crowd.
passages.sermon:
Judas agreed to their plan.
Judas began to look for a chance to betray Jesus.
Judas wanted to do this when there was no crowd present.
Judas wanted to hand Jesus over to the chief priests and temple officers.
passages.original: καὶ ἐξωμολόγησεν καὶ ἐζήτει εὐκαιρίαν τοῦ παραδοῦναι αὐτὸν ἄτερ ὄχλου αὐτοῖς

passages.text: Then came the day of Unleavened Bread on which the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed.
passages.sermon: The day of Unleavened Bread arrived.\r\nOn this day, people had to sacrifice the Passover lamb.
passages.original: Ἦλθεν δὲ ἡ ἡμέρα τῶν ἀζύμων ἐν ᾗ ἔδει θύεσθαι τὸ πάσχα

passages.text: Jesus sent Peter and John, saying, “Go and prepare for us to eat the Passover.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Peter and John.
Jesus sent Peter and John.
Jesus said, “Go.”
Jesus said, “Prepare the Passover for us.”
Jesus said, “We will eat the Passover.”
passages.original: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην εἰπών Πορευθέντες ἑτοιμάσατε ἡμῖν τὸ πάσχα ἵνα φάγωμεν

passages.text: “Where do You want us to prepare it?” they asked.
passages.sermon: Peter and John spoke to Jesus.\r\nThey asked Jesus a question.\r\nThey said, “Where do you want us to prepare the Passover?”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ποῦ θέλεις ἑτοιμάσωμεν

passages.text: He answered, “When you enter the city, a man carrying a jug of water will meet you. Follow him to the house he enters, and say to the owner of that house, ‘The Teacher asks: Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Peter and John.
He gave them instructions.
He said, “When you enter the city, you will meet a man.
This man will carry a jug of water.
Follow this man.
He will go into a house.
Go into that house with him.
Speak to the owner of the house.
Say to the owner, ‘The Teacher asks you a question.’
Say, ‘Where is the guest room?’
Say, ‘I want to eat the Passover there with My disciples.’”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἰδοὺ εἰσελθόντων ὑμῶν εἰς τὴν πόλιν συναντήσει ὑμῖν ἄνθρωπος κεράμιον ὕδατος βαστάζων ἀκολουθήσατε αὐτῷ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν εἰς ἣν εἰσπορεύεται καὶ ἐρεῖτε τῷ οἰκοδεσπότῃ τῆς οἰκίας Λέγει σοι ὁ Διδάσκαλος Ποῦ ἐστιν τὸ κατάλυμα ὅπου τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου φάγω

passages.text: And he will show you a large upper room, already furnished. Make preparations there.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them about a man they would meet in the city.
This man would show them a large upper room.
The room would already have everything ready.
Jesus told His disciples to prepare the Passover meal in that room.
passages.original: κἀκεῖνος ὑμῖν δείξει ἀνάγαιον μέγα ἐστρωμένον ἐκεῖ ἑτοιμάσατε

passages.text: So they went and found it just as Jesus had told them. And they prepared the Passover.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He gave them instructions.
The disciples left.
They went to the city.
They found everything exactly as Jesus had told them.
They prepared the Passover meal.
passages.original: Ἀπελθόντες δὲ εὗρον καθὼς εἰρήκει αὐτοῖς καὶ ἡτοίμασαν τὸ πάσχα

passages.text: When the hour had come, Jesus reclined at the table with His apostles.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with His apostles.
The time arrived.
Jesus sat down at the table.
The apostles sat with Him.
passages.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡ ὥρα ἀνέπεσεν καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι σὺν αὐτῷ

passages.text: And He said to them, “I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before My suffering.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His apostles.\r\nJesus said, “I have greatly desired to eat this Passover meal with you.\r\nI want to do this before I suffer.”
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἐπεθύμησα τοῦτο τὸ πάσχα φαγεῖν μεθ’ ὑμῶν πρὸ τοῦ με παθεῖν

passages.text: For I tell you that I will not eat it again until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His apostles.
Jesus said, “I tell you this truth.
I will not eat this Passover again.
I will wait until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.”
passages.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐκέτι οὐ μὴ φάγω αὐτὸ ἕως ὅτου πληρωθῇ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: After taking the cup, He gave thanks and said, “Take this and divide it among yourselves.
passages.sermon:
Jesus sat with His disciples.
He took a cup.
He gave thanks to God.
He spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Take this cup.
Divide it among yourselves.”
passages.original: Καὶ δεξάμενος ποτήριον εὐχαριστήσας εἶπεν Λάβετε τοῦτο καὶ διαμερίσατε εἰς ἑαυτούς

passages.text: For I tell you that I will not drink of the fruit of the vine from now on until the kingdom of God comes.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “I tell you this truth.
I will not drink the fruit of the vine again from this moment.
I will wait until the kingdom of God comes.
Only then will I drink it again.”
passages.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ πίω ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου ἕως οὗ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ ἔλθῃ

passages.text: And He took the bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus sat with His disciples.
He took bread.
He gave thanks to God.
He broke the bread.
He gave the bread to His disciples.
He spoke to them.
He said, “This bread is My body.”
He said, “My body is given for you.”
He said, “Do this to remember Me.”
passages.original: Καὶ λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν διδόμενον τοῦτο ποιεῖτε εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν

passages.text: In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus sat with His disciples after supper.
He took the cup.
He spoke to them.
He said, “This cup is the new covenant.
This covenant is in My blood.
My blood is poured out for you.”
passages.original: καὶ τὸ ποτήριον ὡσαύτως μετὰ τὸ δειπνῆσαι λέγων Τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη ἐν τῷ αἵματί μου τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐκχυννόμενον

passages.text: Look! The hand of My betrayer is with Mine on the table.
passages.sermon:
Jesus sat at the table with His disciples.
He spoke to them.
He said, “Look!”
He said, “The hand of My betrayer is with Mine on the table.”
passages.original: Πλὴν ἰδοὺ ἡ χεὶρ τοῦ παραδιδόντος με μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς τραπέζης

passages.text: Indeed, the Son of Man will go as it has been determined, but woe to that man who betrays Him.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
God has already decided what will happen to Jesus.
Jesus will go as God has determined.
But there will be trouble for the man who betrays Jesus.
Woe to that man who hands Jesus over.
passages.original: ὅτι ὁ Υἱὸς μὲν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου κατὰ τὸ ὡρισμένον πορεύεται πλὴν οὐαὶ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ δι’ οὗ παραδίδοται

passages.text: Then they began to question among themselves which of them was going to do this.
passages.sermon:
The disciples sat with Jesus at the table.
Jesus said someone would betray Him.
The disciples heard this.
They began to talk to each other.
They asked which one of them would do this thing.
They wondered who would betray Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ αὐτοὶ ἤρξαντο συζητεῖν πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς τὸ τίς ἄρα εἴη ἐξ αὐτῶν ὁ τοῦτο μέλλων πράσσειν

passages.text: A dispute also arose among the disciples as to which of them would be considered the greatest.
passages.sermon:
The disciples followed Jesus.
A dispute arose among the disciples.
They argued with each other.
They wanted to know which one of them was the greatest.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ καὶ φιλονεικία ἐν αὐτοῖς τὸ τίς αὐτῶν δοκεῖ εἶναι μείζων

passages.text: So Jesus declared, “The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those in authority over them call themselves benefactors.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to his disciples.\r\nHe said, "The kings of the Gentiles rule over their people.\r\nThose who have authority over them call themselves benefactors."
passages.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Οἱ βασιλεῖς τῶν ἐθνῶν κυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ ἐξουσιάζοντες αὐτῶν εὐεργέται καλοῦνται

passages.text: But you shall not be like them. Instead, the greatest among you should be like the youngest, and the one who leads like the one who serves.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “You must not act like the Gentile rulers.
Do not imitate those who seek power over others.
The greatest person among you must become like the youngest.
The leader among you must become like the one who serves.”
passages.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐχ οὕτως ἀλλ’ ὁ μείζων ἐν ὑμῖν γινέσθω ὡς ὁ νεώτερος καὶ ὁ ἡγούμενος ὡς ὁ διακονῶν

passages.text: For who is greater, the one who reclines at the table or the one who serves? Is it not the one who reclines? But I am among you as one who serves.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Who is greater?”
He gave two choices.
He said, “Is it the one who reclines at the table?”
He also said, “Or is it the one who serves?”
He answered His own question.
He said, “Is it not the one who reclines at the table?”
Jesus then spoke about Himself.
He said, “But I am among you as one who serves.”
passages.original: τίς γὰρ μείζων ὁ ἀνακείμενος ἢ ὁ διακονῶν οὐχὶ ὁ ἀνακείμενος ἐγὼ δὲ ἐν μέσῳ ὑμῶν εἰμι ὡς ὁ διακονῶν

passages.text: You are the ones who have stood by Me in My trials.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His disciples.
You are the ones who have stayed with Me.
You remained with Me during My trials.
You did not leave Me when I faced difficulties.
You stood by Me in times of testing.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς δέ ἐστε οἱ διαμεμενηκότες μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐν τοῖς πειρασμοῖς μου

passages.text: And I bestow on you a kingdom, just as My Father has bestowed one on Me, so that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom, and sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “My Father gave Me a kingdom.
Now I give you a kingdom, just as My Father gave one to Me.
You will eat at My table in My kingdom.
You will drink at My table in My kingdom.
You will sit on thrones in My kingdom.
You will judge the twelve tribes of Israel.”
passages.original: κἀγὼ διατίθεμαι ὑμῖν καθὼς διέθετό μοι ὁ Πατήρ μου βασιλείαν ἵνα ἔσθητε καὶ πίνητε ἐπὶ τῆς τραπέζης μου ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ μου καὶ καθήσεσθε ἐπὶ θρόνων τὰς δώδεκα φυλὰς κρίνοντες τοῦ Ἰσραήλ

passages.text: Simon, Simon, Satan has asked to sift each of you like wheat.
passages.sermon:
Simon, you are one of My disciples.
Simon, listen carefully.
Satan is the enemy of God and of you.
Satan has asked for permission to test all of you.
He wants to shake you and separate you, just as a farmer sifts wheat.
passages.original: Σίμων Σίμων ἰδοὺ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐξῃτήσατο ὑμᾶς τοῦ σινιάσαι ὡς τὸν σῖτον

passages.text: But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail. And when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Simon Peter.
Jesus said, “I have prayed for you, Simon.
I prayed that your faith will not fail.
You will turn back to Me one day.
When you return, strengthen your brothers.”
passages.original: ἐγὼ δὲ ἐδεήθην περὶ σοῦ ἵνα μὴ ἐκλίπῃ ἡ πίστις σου καὶ σύ ποτε ἐπιστρέψας στήρισον τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου

passages.text: “Lord,” said Peter, “I am ready to go with You even to prison and to death.”
passages.sermon:
Peter spoke to Jesus.
Peter called Jesus “Lord.”
Peter said he was ready to go with Jesus.
Peter said he was ready to go with Jesus to prison.
Peter said he was ready to go with Jesus to death.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Κύριε μετὰ σοῦ ἕτοιμός εἰμι καὶ εἰς φυλακὴν καὶ εἰς θάνατον πορεύεσθαι

passages.text: But Jesus replied, “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today until you have denied three times that you know Me.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to Peter.\r\nJesus said, “Peter, I tell you this.\r\nToday, before the rooster crows, you will deny three times that you know Me.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Λέγω σοι Πέτρε οὐ φωνήσει σήμερον ἀλέκτωρ ἕως τρίς με ἀπαρνήσῃ μὴ εἰδέναι

passages.text: Then Jesus asked them, “When I sent you out without purse or bag or sandals, did you lack anything?” “Nothing,” they answered.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He reminded them of a past event.
He said, “I sent you out before.”
He said, “You had no purse.”
He said, “You had no bag.”
He said, “You had no sandals.”
He asked, “Did you lack anything?”
The disciples answered Him.
They said, “Nothing.”
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὅτε ἀπέστειλα ὑμᾶς ἄτερ βαλλαντίου καὶ πήρας καὶ ὑποδημάτων μή τινος ὑστερήσατε Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Οὐθενός

passages.text: “Now, however,” He told them, “the one with a purse should take it, and likewise a bag; and the one without a sword should sell his cloak and buy one.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, "Now things are different."
If you have a purse, take it with you.
If you have a bag, take it also.
If you do not have a sword, sell your cloak.
Buy a sword with the money from your cloak.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς Ἀλλὰ νῦν ὁ ἔχων βαλλάντιον ἀράτω ὁμοίως καὶ πήραν καὶ ὁ μὴ ἔχων πωλησάτω τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀγορασάτω μάχαιραν

passages.text: For I tell you that this Scripture must be fulfilled in Me: ‘And He was numbered with the transgressors.’ For what is written about Me is reaching its fulfillment.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus said, “I tell you this truth.
This Scripture must be fulfilled in Me.
The Scripture says, ‘He was numbered with the transgressors.’
This means people will count Me among sinners.
What is written about Me is coming true now.
Everything written about Me is reaching its fulfillment.”
passages.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι τοῦτο τὸ γεγραμμένον δεῖ τελεσθῆναι ἐν ἐμοί Τό Καὶ μετὰ ἀνόμων ἐλογίσθη καὶ γὰρ τὸ περὶ ἐμοῦ τέλος ἔχει

passages.text: So they said, “Look, Lord, here are two swords.” “That is enough,” He answered.
passages.sermon:
The disciples spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Lord, look. Here are two swords.”
Jesus answered them.
He said, “That is enough.”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Κύριε ἰδοὺ μάχαιραι ὧδε δύο Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἱκανόν ἐστιν

passages.text: Jesus went out as usual to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples followed Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus left the place.
He went to the Mount of Olives.
He did this often.
His disciples followed Him.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη κατὰ τὸ ἔθος εἰς τὸ ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν ἠκολούθησαν δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ μαθηταί

passages.text: When He came to the place, He told them, “Pray that you will not enter into temptation.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus arrived at the place.
He spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Pray.”
He said, “Do not enter into temptation.”
passages.original: γενόμενος δὲ ἐπὶ τοῦ τόπου εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Προσεύχεσθε μὴ εἰσελθεῖν εἰς πειρασμόν

passages.text: And He withdrew about a stone’s throw beyond them, where He knelt down and prayed, “Father, if You are willing, take this cup from Me. Yet not My will, but Yours be done.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
\r\nJesus left His disciples.
\r\nHe went a short distance away.
\r\nHe went about as far as someone can throw a stone.
\r\nJesus knelt down.
\r\nHe prayed.
\r\nHe said, “Father, if You are willing, take this cup from Me.”
\r\nHe also said, “Yet not My will, but Yours be done.”
passages.original: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἀπεσπάσθη ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὡσεὶ λίθου βολήν καὶ θεὶς τὰ γόνατα προσηύχετο λέγων Πάτερ εἰ βούλει παρένεγκε τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ πλὴν μὴ τὸ θέλημά μου ἀλλὰ τὸ σὸν γινέσθω

passages.text: Then an angel from heaven appeared to Him and strengthened Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus prayed in great anguish.
An angel came down from heaven.
The angel appeared to Jesus.
The angel strengthened Jesus.
passages.original: Ὤφθη δὲ αὐτῷ ἄγγελος ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ ἐνισχύων αὐτόν

passages.text: And in His anguish, He prayed more earnestly, and His sweat became like drops of blood falling to the ground.
passages.sermon:
Jesus felt deep anguish.
He prayed more earnestly.
His sweat became like drops of blood.
The drops of blood fell to the ground.
passages.original: καὶ γενόμενος ἐν ἀγωνίᾳ ἐκτενέστερον προσηύχετο καὶ ἐγένετο ὁ ἱδρὼς αὐτοῦ ὡσεὶ θρόμβοι αἵματος καταβαίνοντες ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν

passages.text: When Jesus rose from prayer and returned to the disciples, He found them asleep, exhausted from sorrow.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had been praying.
He stood up after He finished praying.
He went to His disciples.
He found His disciples sleeping.
They were sleeping because they were very sad.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀναστὰς ἀπὸ τῆς προσευχῆς ἐλθὼν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς εὗρεν κοιμωμένους αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς λύπης

passages.text: “Why are you sleeping?” He asked. “Get up and pray so that you will not enter into temptation.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He found them sleeping.
He said, “Why are you sleeping?”
He told them, “Get up.”
He told them, “Pray.”
He warned them, “Pray so that you will not enter into temptation.”
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τί καθεύδετε ἀναστάντες προσεύχεσθε ἵνα μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς πειρασμόν

passages.text: While He was still speaking, a crowd arrived, led by the man called Judas, one of the Twelve. He approached Jesus to kiss Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was still speaking.
A crowd arrived.
Judas led the crowd.
Judas was one of the Twelve disciples.
Judas came near to Jesus.
Judas approached Jesus to kiss Him.
passages.original: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ ὄχλος καὶ ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν δώδεκα προήρχετο αὐτούς καὶ ἤγγισεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ φιλῆσαι αὐτόν

passages.text: But Jesus asked him, “Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Judas.
Judas was one of the twelve disciples.
Jesus said, “Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?”
The Son of Man means Jesus Himself.
Judas used a kiss to show who Jesus was to the crowd.
Judas chose to betray Jesus in this way.
passages.original: Ἰησοῦς δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἰούδα φιλήματι τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδως

passages.text: Those around Jesus saw what was about to happen and said, “Lord, should we strike with our swords?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood with His disciples.
A crowd approached Jesus.
Judas, one of the Twelve disciples, led the crowd.
The people near Jesus saw what would happen next.
These people spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Lord, should we strike with our swords?”
passages.original: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ περὶ αὐτὸν τὸ ἐσόμενον εἶπαν Κύριε εἰ πατάξομεν ἐν μαχαίρῃ

passages.text: And one of them struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his right ear.
passages.sermon:
One man stood with Jesus.
This man used a sword.
He struck the servant of the high priest.
He cut off the servant’s right ear.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπάταξεν εἷς τις ἐξ αὐτῶν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως τὸν δοῦλον καὶ ἀφεῖλεν τὸ οὖς αὐτοῦ τὸ δεξιόν

passages.text: But Jesus answered, “No more of this!” And He touched the man’s ear and healed him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke.
Jesus said, “No more of this.”
Jesus touched the man’s ear.
Jesus healed the man.
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Ἐᾶτε ἕως τούτου καὶ ἁψάμενος τοῦ ὠτίου ἰάσατο αὐτόν

passages.text: Then Jesus said to the chief priests, temple officers, and elders who had come for Him, “Have you come out with swords and clubs as you would against an outlaw?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the chief priests.
He spoke to the temple officers.
He spoke to the elders.
These men had come to arrest Jesus.
Jesus said, “You have come out to seize me.
You brought swords and clubs.
You act as if I am an outlaw.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς τοὺς παραγενομένους ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ στρατηγοὺς τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ πρεσβυτέρους Ὡς ἐπὶ λῃστὴν ἐξήλθατε μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων

passages.text: Every day I was with you in the temple courts, and you did not lay a hand on Me. But this hour belongs to you and to the power of darkness.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the chief priests, temple officers, and elders.
He said, “Every day I was with you in the temple courts.
You did not arrest Me then.
Now this is your hour.
Now the power of darkness has control.”
passages.original: καθ’ ἡμέραν ὄντος μου μεθ’ ὑμῶν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ οὐκ ἐξετείνατε τὰς χεῖρας ἐπ’ ἐμέ ἀλλ’ αὕτη ἐστὶν ὑμῶν ἡ ὥρα καὶ ἡ ἐξουσία τοῦ σκότους

passages.text: Then they seized Jesus, led Him away, and took Him into the house of the high priest. And Peter followed at a distance.
passages.sermon:
The men seized Jesus.
They led Jesus away.
They took Jesus into the house of the high priest.
Peter followed Jesus.
Peter stayed far behind.
passages.original: Συλλαβόντες δὲ αὐτὸν ἤγαγον καὶ εἰσήγαγον εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἠκολούθει μακρόθεν

passages.text: When those present had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat down among them.
passages.sermon:
People gathered in the courtyard.
They started a fire in the middle of the courtyard.
They all sat down together around the fire.
Peter sat down among them.
passages.original: Περιαψάντων δὲ πῦρ ἐν μέσῳ τῆς αὐλῆς καὶ συνκαθισάντων ἐκάθητο ὁ Πέτρος μέσος αὐτῶν

passages.text: A servant girl saw him seated in the firelight and looked intently at him. “This man also was with Him,” she said.
passages.sermon:
A servant girl saw Peter.
Peter sat near the firelight.
The girl looked closely at Peter.
She spoke about Peter.
She said, “This man was also with Jesus.”
passages.original: ἰδοῦσα δὲ αὐτὸν παιδίσκη τις καθήμενον πρὸς τὸ φῶς καὶ ἀτενίσασα αὐτῷ εἶπεν Καὶ οὗτος σὺν αὐτῷ ἦν

passages.text: But Peter denied it. “Woman, I do not know Him,” he said.
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter sat among the people in the courtyard.
A servant girl said Peter was with Jesus.
Peter denied her claim.
Peter said, “Woman, I do not know Him.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἠρνήσατο λέγων Οὐκ οἶδα αὐτόν γύναι

passages.text: A short time later, someone else saw him and said, “You also are one of them.” But Peter said, “Man, I am not.”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter sat near the fire.
A short time passed.
Another person saw Peter.
This person spoke to Peter.
He said, "You also are one of them."
Peter answered him.
Peter said, "Man, I am not."
passages.original: Καὶ μετὰ βραχὺ ἕτερος ἰδὼν αὐτὸν ἔφη Καὶ σὺ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶ Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἔφη Ἄνθρωπε οὐκ εἰμί

passages.text: About an hour later, another man insisted, “Certainly this man was with Him, for he too is a Galilean.”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
About an hour passed.
Another man saw Peter.
This man spoke with confidence.
He said, “This man was certainly with Jesus.”
He explained, “He is also a Galilean.”
passages.original: Καὶ διαστάσης ὡσεὶ ὥρας μιᾶς ἄλλος τις διϊσχυρίζετο λέγων Ἐπ’ ἀληθείας καὶ οὗτος μετ’ αὐτοῦ ἦν καὶ γὰρ Γαλιλαῖός ἐστιν

passages.text: “Man, I do not know what you are talking about,” Peter replied. While he was still speaking, the rooster crowed.
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter spoke to the man.
Peter said, “Man, I do not know what you are talking about.”
Peter was still speaking.
The rooster crowed.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος Ἄνθρωπε οὐκ οἶδα ὃ λέγεις καὶ παραχρῆμα ἔτι λαλοῦντος αὐτοῦ ἐφώνησεν ἀλέκτωρ

passages.text: And the Lord turned and looked at Peter. Then Peter remembered the word that the Lord had spoken to him: “Before the rooster crows today, you will deny Me three times.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Lord.
Peter is a disciple of Jesus.
Jesus turned and looked at Peter.
Peter remembered something important.
Jesus had spoken a word to Peter earlier.
Jesus said to Peter, “Before the rooster crows today, you will deny Me three times.”
passages.original: καὶ στραφεὶς ὁ Κύριος ἐνέβλεψεν τῷ Πέτρῳ καὶ ὑπεμνήσθη ὁ Πέτρος τοῦ λόγου τοῦ Κυρίου ὡς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὅτι Πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι σήμερον ἀπαρνήσῃ με τρίς

passages.text: And he went outside and wept bitterly.
passages.sermon:
Peter left the place.
He went outside.
Peter cried very hard.
He wept bitterly.
passages.original: καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἔξω ἔκλαυσεν πικρῶς

passages.text: The men who were holding Jesus began to mock Him and beat Him.
passages.sermon: The men held Jesus.\r\nThese men began to mock Jesus.\r\nThey beat Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ συνέχοντες αὐτὸν ἐνέπαιζον αὐτῷ δέροντες

passages.text: They blindfolded Him and kept demanding, “Prophesy! Who hit You?”
passages.sermon:
The men held Jesus.
They blindfolded Jesus.
They questioned Jesus again and again.
They said, “Prophesy!”
They asked, “Who hit you?”
passages.original: καὶ περικαλύψαντες αὐτὸν ἐπηρώτων λέγοντες Προφήτευσον τίς ἐστιν ὁ παίσας σε

passages.text: And they said many other blasphemous things against Him.
passages.sermon: The men held Jesus.\r\nThey spoke many blasphemous things against Him.\r\nThey said other evil things to Him.
passages.original: καὶ ἕτερα πολλὰ βλασφημοῦντες ἔλεγον εἰς αὐτόν

passages.text: At daybreak the council of the elders of the people, both the chief priests and scribes, met together. They led Jesus into their Sanhedrin and said, “If You are the Christ, tell us.” Jesus answered, “If I tell you, you will not believe.
passages.sermon:
At daybreak, the council of the elders gathered.
The chief priests and scribes were there.
They brought Jesus to their council.
They spoke to Jesus.
They said, “If you are the Christ, tell us.”
Jesus answered them.
He said, “If I tell you, you will not believe.”
passages.original: Καὶ ὡς ἐγένετο ἡμέρα συνήχθη τὸ πρεσβυτέριον τοῦ λαοῦ ἀρχιερεῖς τε καὶ γραμματεῖς καὶ ἀπήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ συνέδριον αὐτῶν λέγοντες Εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστός εἰπὸν ἡμῖν Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς Ἐὰν ὑμῖν εἴπω οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε

passages.text: And if I ask you a question, you will not answer.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the council of elders.
The chief priests and scribes were present.
Jesus spoke to them directly.
He said, “If I ask you a question, you will not answer.”
passages.original: ἐὰν δὲ ἐρωτήσω οὐ μὴ ἀποκριθῆτε

passages.text: But from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the council of elders, chief priests, and scribes.
They questioned Jesus about His identity as the Christ.
Jesus said, “From now on, the Son of Man will sit at the right hand of God’s power.”
Jesus identified Himself as the Son of Man.
God’s power is supreme.
The right hand of God is a place of highest honor and authority.
Jesus declared that He would take this place of honor and authority.
passages.original: ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν δὲ ἔσται ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καθήμενος ἐκ δεξιῶν τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: So they all asked, “Are You then the Son of God?” He replied, “You say that I am.”
passages.sermon:
The council questioned Jesus.
They asked Him a direct question.
They said, "Are you the Son of God?"
Jesus answered them.
He said, "You say that I am."
passages.original: Εἶπαν δὲ πάντες Σὺ οὖν εἶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ Ὁ δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἔφη Ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι

passages.text: “Why do we need any more testimony?” they declared. “We have heard it for ourselves from His own lips.”
passages.sermon:
The council spoke together.
They said, “Why do we need any more testimony?”
They explained their reason.
They said, “We have heard it ourselves.”
They said, “We heard it from His own lips.”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Τί ἔτι ἔχομεν μαρτυρίας χρείαν αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἠκούσαμεν ἀπὸ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ
